gen-dafont-groovy-gf-huninn: Groovy nearly seals its c into a slit, funky and friendly. Huninn keeps its s terminals clear of the body and its crossbars as sturdy as the stems, so paragraphs move along easily.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-kufam: Body text flows like one neon tube, far from the pinched c in Groovy. Kufam opens its e generously and lets the bodies dominate each line while ascenders hardly show, so long paragraphs feel easy-going.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-lexend: Body text reads big and open-jawed, unlike the tight funk of Groovy. Lexend keeps its stroke thickness steady around every curve, and its outsized lowercase makes paragraphs feel approachable.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-mada: Body text stands tall in the middle and never quite closes its curves, unlike Groovy, which has no hairlines at all. Mada stays approachable and modern line after line.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-maven-pro: Groovy pinches its c to a narrow slit and spreads its lowercase loosely, all friendly funk. Maven Pro leaves a welcoming gap in its c and keeps its line gentle, so the two sit easily together.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-miriam-libre: Funky and pinched up top, wiry and open below. Groovy nearly seals its c, while Miriam Libre keeps its s generously open, so paragraphs read with wiry, easy confidence.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-mochiy-pop-p-one: Groovy pinches its c nearly shut and sprawls its lowercase loosely. Mochiy Pop P One spaces its sizable lowercase far apart and skips any brush-like swell, so the two share a page happily.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-montserrat-underlin: Pinched, loose and funky, Groovy nearly seals its c and spaces its lowercase out. Montserrat Underline keeps its round bowls uniform and its counters wide, so paragraphs read big and open.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-nobile: Groovy nearly seals its c and keeps its arms and legs constant-width, with no thin hairline against a thick stem. Groovy supplies the funk; Nobile supplies open, cap-hugging lowercase.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans: Friendly and funky, Groovy nearly seals its c and spaces its lowercase loosely, with joins as slim as a pipe cleaner. Noto Sans, meanwhile, fills most of the letter height, so paragraphs read smoothly.
